title: Delacroix (Paris) to Létombe (Philadelphia), despatch No. 5, 25 Messidor an V / 13 July 1797 (NARA M30 roll 4, frames 0244-0245)

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Great Britain, vol. 5, M30 roll 4, frames 0244 right, 0245

plaintext.source: The ministry's clear draft (minute) of the despatch: Archives diplomatiques, Correspondance politique, États-Unis, vol. 48 (39CP/48), ff. 41r-42r, marked 'à chiffrer. F.' and 'Politique N° 5'; found by Andrew Beling on 21 Nov 2026 (PR #884). It is the draft, not the copy sent: one clause of it has no groups in the American copy. No decipherment on NARA frames 0236-0252; King's No. 53: 'I have no means of decyphering it.'

system.summary: A numeric code of groups up to 1198 for words, syllables, single letters and names, with homophones; short alphabetical runs placed in an order that is not alphabetical. A partial table (297 numbers, 136 confirmed by two or more agreeing uses) was built from the ministry's clear draft (Andrew Beling, PR #884).
system.notes: From the contributor's partial table (beling2026/README.md, 'What the code looks like'): number order and alphabetical order do not agree over the whole table (Spearman 0.08), but 76% of adjacent pairs ascend; full stops have numbers (412, 413, 416, 417); 469 is aligned to nothing at the head of the text. 148 values rest on one use in this one letter. The 2 Nov inference of homophones in small numeric blocks agrees with the table (81-83 a, 972-973 de, 265-269 le/les).

prior_solution.where: No reading of the copy in code was found anywhere. The plaintext survives as the ministry's clear draft, Archives diplomatiques, CP États-Unis vol. 48, ff. 41r-42r (online viewer). Not known on 2 Nov 2026, when the ciphertext-only attempt was made. Found by Andrew Beling's AI agent on 21 Nov 2026: f. 41r first opened 00:52:04 EST (its request log); two blind AI readers transcribed it 01:07-01:13 EST; the test plan was written and hashed 01:31 EST and the test text fixed 01:32 EST, by an agent that, by its own record, had seen the two readers' short reports but not the draft's wording. The order rests on local file times and SHA-256 sums only, no outside timestamp. The reading is the draft laid on the groups.

tools: contributor: EM alignment and held-out test (beling2026/scripts/)

solution.what: Downloaded NARA frames 0243-0245 and viewed the layout; read issue #122.
Adopted Brackx's transcription: 653 groups, 297 distinct, measured.
Read Létombe's reply No. 42 in Turner 1904: part of No. 5 probably concerns keeping his correspondence. No. 5 not printed.
Adjacent-value test: 162 against a random mean of 98 (3,000 trials, none as high).
One-part annealer keeping numeric order alphabetical, Turner 5-gram.
Near-repeat search with aligned differences up to 3: neighbouring numbers interchange in repeated passages.
Hand phrase matching of repeats: République/gouvernement, correspondance politique, confiance, puissance; several retracted, none verified.
Homophonic syllable annealer with character model, tie bonus, length cap, overuse penalty.
Synthetic letters with known keys: true key 802-1338, annealed junk 1692-1789; the character objective cannot find the key.

Word-bigram Viterbi objective separates truth from junk on synthetic letters, with test text in the training corpus; search reaches token accuracy at most 0.037 unpinned, 0.60-0.65 with 51-53% of tokens pinned.
Real text under word-bigram objective, cribs République, gouvernement, nonsense control: both cribs about -2130, control about -2275; cribs not separated; no output reads.
Tenfold-longer unpinned word-bigram run on synthetic letters: token accuracy at most 0.028.
Word-placement moves with diversity constraints on synthetic letters: at most 0.031 from scratch; pinning the top 80 groups adds only 3-6 points above the pinned share.
Strict one-part test with blocks: held-out synthetic letters -1818 to -2096 at accuracy about 0.5; real -2527 to -2719; scrambled numbers -2596 to -2810. One-part not supported.
Alphabetical only inside blocks of 100 or 25: real and scrambled numbers indistinguishable.
Two-part search with consecutive numbers merged: synthetic accuracy at most 0.017; real output not readable.
Seven French numeric keys in the repo applied against 50 permuted copies each: all within chance.
Web searches; Schnakenbourg 2026 paywalled; CADN Philadelphia finding aid: 519PO/1 art. 1 holds incoming ministry letters March 1793-Feb 1798.

Contributor (Andrew Beling, with AI agents, PR #884): the ministry's clear draft of No. 5 found in the Archives diplomatiques online viewer, CP États-Unis vol. 48, ff. 41r-42r, marked 'à chiffrer. F.' and 'Politique N° 5'. First opened 21 Nov 2026 00:52:04 EST (the agent's request log). Not seen by the project on the archive's images (the viewer needs JavaScript).

Contributor: the draft transcribed by two blind AI readers (01:07-01:13 EST) and merged; one wording dispute (aurez/avez) went into the test text as reader A's aurez by the plan's rule, and a third AI agent of the contributor's read aurez on the image afterwards. No person has read the draft.

Contributor: test plan written and hashed 01:31 EST, test text fixed 01:32 EST, by the session's own statement before its writer saw the draft's wording (it had seen the readers' short reports) (local file times and SHA-256 only). Test 1, letters per group 3.42 (pass mark 2.0-6.0). Test 2a, repeated runs 0.83 against controls up to 1.00: a miss, reported. Test 2b, full EM alignment 0.77 against 80 controls up to 0.17: pass. Tests 1, 2a, 2b not rerun by the project.

Contributor: table fitted on the first 568 groups and frozen, scored on the last 85: 43 predictions, 36 fit (0.837). The contributor's second scorer (reviewer_heldout.py) rerun at our review of the pull request (round 4): 36 of 43; 1,000 shuffled keys mean 12.3, at most 18.

Contributor: hand alignment of the draft on the 653 groups, made after the tests; partial table on Brackx's digits (297 numbers: 136 class A with two or more agreeing uses, 103 B and 45 B2 on one use, 13 C unsure); decryption, reading and translation. 27 words of the reading carry a mark (444 cipher words by make_reading.py, 442 by the reviewer's count): 0.939. Rebuilt at review: the table and the decryption come out identical.

Contributor: eight digit changes to Brackx's transcription proposed from three blind AI readings of the film each; 898 (3 of 3), 1034 and 527 (2 of 3) supported, five on at most one reader. None applied anywhere; they stay proposals until a person has looked at the film. Not checked on the film by the project.

Integration: strict share computed with strict_share.py from the contributor's alignment, table and proposals file. Of 444 cipher words, 296 rest only on class A values (0.667), 121 touch at least one single-use value (class B or B2) and count as probable, 27 are holes. Token classes 481 A, 103 B, 45 B2, 24 C. Marked groups 29: 8 proposal places, 17 class C, 4 where the group's table value differs from the draft's letters.
Integration: the reading read through as sentences with the decryption beside it (reading_review, grade B). Not done: the draft against the archive images, the film, a rerun of tests 1, 2a, 2b.

Write-up: the catalogue, the leads and every target profile of 1789-1803 searched again for French diplomatic texts in numbers. Found only astrea1799 (Rozier to Talleyrand, 1798; numbers on a Massachusetts Historical Society microfilm) and catalogue 521 (Rivals to Sieyès, 1798, Archives nationales): neither is online. No second text to apply the table to.

Write-up: the partial table compared number by number with every key file under targets/ that lists numbers with values (key_compare.py, 174 files; null: each key's values shuffled over its own numbers, 200 times). The seven French keys of the 2 Nov scan agree on 0 of their 39 to 209 shared numbers; the most any file reaches is 3 of 47 (petkum1665). No key held here is this code.

Write-up: four web searches (the draft's wording; Rozier, Mozard and Hauterive with Létombe; King's No. 53; the ministry's cipher of 1797). No printed or quoted text of No. 5 and no table of the code found.

Write-up: key replay (docs/_replay.py with replay.py). The table applied to the 653 groups and compared with the reading: 441 words by the tool's division (no division at hyphens; 444 by make_reading.py), 414 exact (0.939), 27 marked in the reading (26 listed as marked, one as an i/y difference), no unmarked difference.

Write-up: the Paris volumes. The archive's record pages and search are plain pages (39CP/47, January to June 1797, 938 images; 39CP/48, 841 images); the images open only in its viewer, which in Chrome shows a notice of conditions of reuse with one button to accept. Not accepted on the owner's behalf, so the draft was not seen on the images and 39CP/47 was not paged in full for a text in numbers.

Write-up: the two doubtful single-use numbers 300 and 1105 looked at on the NARA frames at twice their size (an AI reading). Not settled: the last digit of 300 has the same looped form as the last digit of 630 beside it; the third digit of 1105 is a filled loop over show-through. Brackx's digits kept.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 622 tokens, 285 types, fr-modern order 4: reading -1.938 per letter; random keys -2.514 (z 10.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.927 (mean -1.935, z -0.3); annealer on the real text -1.911. Verdict: underdetermined.

texts.summary: Delacroix tells Létombe that the consuls at New York and Boston have sent him President Adams's speech at the opening of the extraordinary session, that he hopes the President does not mean to go to extremes, and that the Directory's position is in his despatch of 29 prairial. He asks for prompt detail on Congress, and orders that consuls keep political matter out of clear despatches, pass it to the agents charged with politics or put it in cipher, since what has already been intercepted must serve as a lesson.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #884 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read beling2026/readings/reading_1797-07-13.md in full as sentences, with the opening lines of the filed decryption beside it: coherent French in every sentence, 27 marked holes, each a short word or part of a word that the sentence carries. Grade B because the words are the ministry's draft laid on the groups (circular by design) and 121 further words rest on single-use values; the strict share is 0.667. The draft was not seen on the archive's images and no person has checked it.

texts.note: Read in part: 0.939 is under the 95% bar. The text is the ministry's draft laid on Brackx's digits by a hand alignment; a clause of the draft (est arrivé à Paris, il y a quinze jours: Il) has no groups in the copy and is not counted. The 'contemporary' file is the clear draft, a separate document in Paris, not a decipherment of the copy.

outcome.notes: Verification: the clear draft is also the source of the table, so it confirms nothing by itself; the evidence that it is the text behind the groups is the contributor's held-out test (36 of 43 against at most 18 for shuffled keys), not recorded as a statistical test here: the project's own check (docs/_validate.py, 24 Nov 2026) is underdetermined, a key of the same shape fitted to the shuffled groups scores as well as the reading. Owner's decision of 23 Nov 2026: method key recovered from external plaintext, class read in part, single-use values count as probable. The 653 groups are Michael Brackx's transcription from the film (a person's, transcription.by); every reader of the draft is an AI agent; the eight digit proposals rest on the contributor's AI readers; no person has compared the reading with the film. Not checked by the project: the draft against the archive's images (its viewer asks the reader to accept conditions of reuse; not accepted on the owner's behalf), the film for the eight proposals, tests 1, 2a and 2b by rerun. Written up 24 Nov 2026; catalogue 649 removed as written up; no DECODE record is known and the queue entry is a hold until Brackx and Beling agree. Open lead: 39CP/47 in full.
